ns2:course.label: Messaging Strategy
ns2:course.description: Creating and executing successful messages across communication channels. Explores the development of persuasive messaging through theories of persuasion, consumer-information processing and theories of creativity. The course examines the relationship between creative strategy and creative executions while allowing students to practice creating content for traditional and non-traditional media. Strategic brand communication manages every message and contact point within an organization. Audiences include not only consumers, but employees, stockholders, the media, and others. 3 graduate hours. No professional credit. Students may not earn credit for SBC 510, Messaging Strategy, if credit was earned for SBC 508, Messaging Strategy, prior to Spring 2021. Prerequisite: SBC 507.
